title: What If Earth's Fresh Water Were Only Its Rivers and Lakes?

scenes.text: What if Earth's only fresh water was every river and lake you can see?
Start with the oceans. About 96.5 percent of all water on Earth is salt water.
Only about 2.5 percent is fresh, and roughly 69 percent of that is locked in ice caps and glaciers.
Another 30 percent is groundwater, hidden underground. Take both away, and only lakes, swamps and rivers remain.
That is about 0.3 percent of the fresh water. Rivers alone hold roughly 0.0001 percent of all water on Earth.
Everything on the surface that you could swim in is under one hundredth of one percent of Earth's water.
